newsitem.title: UK: N.Ireland prisoners scale down Belfast jail row.
newsitem.headline: N.Ireland prisoners scale down Belfast jail row.

text.p: Protestant "Loyalist" prisoners came down from the rooftops at a troubled Northern Irish prison on Wednesday as authorities sought to end a two-day protest about new security procedures.

But prison sources said staff who were withdrawn for their own protection on Tuesday had not yet been sent back into two wings of Belfast's Maze prison where the trouble flared 24 hours earlier. They said they would not consider the dispute over until officers returned and reassumed control.

John White of the Ulster Democratic Party, which has links with the jailed pro-British guerrillas, said he would have talks later with a chief official of Britain's Northern Ireland Office, the department that runs the province.

"The prisoners have come down off the roof and returned to their wings. The electricity supply has been restored and I am hoping that food and medication can be delivered to the prisoners," he told BBC radio.

"I am hoping that a line of communication can be installed whereby the prisoners can speak to the prison staff. At this moment, the prison staff are not prepared to go into the wings to talk to the prisoners."
Overnight British officials had urged prison staff to step up personal security after outlawed "Loyalist" militants threatened violence if the authorities used force to end the dispute.

The protesters, called loyalist because of their fierce allegiance to continued British rule, tried to burn down two watchtowers on Tuesday and started another fire on Wednesday when they clambered on to the roof in the early hours.
The pro-British Ulster Freedom Fighters (UFF) warned on Tuesday that they would retaliate if prison riot squads were sent in to break up the protest which involves some of their members.
They said prison staff and civil servants would "pay a price" if the inmates were subjected to "brutal treatment".
A government source said that "staff are being advised to be especially conscious of their personal safety".
The UFF is one of several groups which are pledged to defend British rule against Irish IRA guerrillas.
The prisoners are protesting at tightened security measures brought in after the discovery last month of an escape tunnel in another part of the Maze dug by Irish Republican Army (IRA) prisoners.
Loyalists at the jail say that they are being unfairly punished for the IRA's wrong-doing.
The Maze is Europe's biggest guerrilla prison complex, housing some 500 inmates, segregated according to allegiance.
The tunnel discovery foiled a mass escape plan by the republicans, security sources said then.
